report.tagline: A 10-minute grocery and essentials delivery app, with its own quick café, racing to grow fast and reach profit before its stock market listing.
report.simpleSummary: Zepto is an app where you order groceries, snacks, beauty products and even hot coffee, and it reaches you in about 10 minutes. It was started in 2021 by two 19-year-olds who left Stanford. It keeps small warehouses close to homes so riders only travel about 2 km. It is India's second-biggest quick delivery app by orders, but it still loses a lot of money and has delayed its stock market listing to 2027.

overview.whatItDoes: Zepto delivers groceries, fresh food, household items, beauty, electronics and café food like coffee and sandwiches in about 10 minutes. It runs about 1,100 dark stores in big and mid-sized Indian cities. It filed for an IPO in 2026 but paused it in August 2026 after investors offered a much lower value, and now aims to list by around May 2027.
howItWorks: Zepto runs dark stores, small warehouses closed to walk-in shoppers, each serving homes about 2 km around it. Average delivery distance fell to 1.83 km by early 2026.
Store staff pick and pack orders in a couple of minutes using a layout designed for speed.
Riders pick up the bag and deliver it, so most orders arrive in about 10 minutes.
Zepto Cafe counters inside many stores make tea, coffee and snacks for 10-minute food delivery.
Brands pay Zepto to show their products higher in the app, which has become a big money maker.
Zepto offers deals and a membership plan (Zepto Pass) to make users order more often.
overview.valueProposition: Get daily needs and a hot snack in about 10 minutes, with lots of deals, from an app that feels quick and simple.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Shows how many minutes delivery will take and delivers from a store about 2 km away.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Speed is Zepto's main promise and the reason people install it.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Fresh tea, coffee, sandwiches and snacks made in the dark store and delivered in minutes; also a separate Zepto Cafe app.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Café items have better margins and bring users back daily, not just weekly.

coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Locks in heavy users and makes them order more often from Zepto instead of rivals.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: About 50,000 items per store by early 2026, up from about 12,000 in FY24, including electronics, beauty and toys.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: More items mean bigger baskets and more reasons to open the app.

coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Builds trust in speed and handles problems without phone calls.

businessModel.summary: Zepto earns from the margin on goods it sells, ad money from brands, fees and memberships from customers, and café food sales. In FY26 it still lost about ₹79 on every order after paying riders, stores and discounts. Its plan is to cut that loss using ads, café sales and busier stores.

revenueStreams.detail: Zepto earns the gap between what it pays for goods and what customers pay. This is most of the ₹22,624 crore revenue.
₹1,636 crore in FY26. Brands buy search and banner spots; they report 5 to 8 times return on ad spend.
Freshly made drinks and snacks, which earn more per item than packaged groceries.
Delivery, handling and small cart fees, plus paid membership.

businessModel.pricing: Products at or below MRP with frequent discounts. Delivery is free above a basket limit (often around ₹99 to ₹199 depending on city and membership). Small-cart and handling fees apply at times. Zepto Pass price varies by city and offer. Exact fees not public.
costDrivers: Delivery and handling: ₹3,046 crore in FY26, up over 90%
Dark-store rent, staff and cold storage
Advertising and promotions: ₹1,389 crore in FY26
Discounts to win users from Blinkit and Instamart
Wastage of fresh food and café ingredients
businessModel.unitEconomics: In FY26 Zepto spent about ₹128 to serve each order (down from ₹159 in FY24). On an average order of about ₹500 to ₹550 (estimate), it earns roughly ₹90 to ₹100 from product margin, ads and fees. So it loses money on each order: its own number is about ₹79 lost per order after all running costs (adjusted EBITDA). The loss is shrinking because riders travel shorter distances, stores get busier, and ad revenue grows. Zepto must cut this to zero before investors will pay a high price in an IPO.

howTheyGetUsers: Opening new dark stores in new areas and cities
Youthful brand marketing on Instagram and YouTube
Zepto Cafe as a new reason to try the app
whatBringsUsersBack: Daily café habit for coffee and snacks
Zepto Pass makes free delivery feel worth using often
Order Again list for daily items
Fast and reliable delivery builds trust
growth.moat: Zepto's moat is still being built. Its strengths are tight store locations (short 1.8 km trips), a fast-growing ads business and Zepto Cafe, which rivals copied but Zepto scaled first. But Blinkit is bigger and already profitable, so Zepto's edge depends on executing better, not on something rivals cannot copy.

competitors.name: Blinkit
competitors.positioning: Market leader owned by Eternal (Zomato), with about 46% share and EBITDA profit.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Zepto is smaller (640 million vs 917 million orders in FY26) and loss-making, but pushes café food harder and is seen as more aggressive on deals.

competitors.name: Swiggy Instamart
competitors.positioning: Quick commerce inside Swiggy's food app, sold with Swiggy One.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Zepto has more orders than Instamart (640 million vs 412 million) and is a stand-alone brand, but lacks a food-delivery app to cross-sell from.

competitors.name: Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Zepto is focused only on speed and daily needs; the giants have deeper pockets and huge existing users.

competitors.name: Starbucks, Third Wave Coffee and local cafés
competitors.positioning: Coffee chains with sit-in and delivery through food apps.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Zepto Cafe is cheaper and faster for delivery, but offers no place to sit and a narrower menu.

northStar.metric: Weekly orders delivered on time and complete per active customer
northStar.why: It shows whether users are building a habit with Zepto and getting what they ordered fast. More reliable repeat orders also make stores busier and cut loss per order.

improvementIdeas.idea: One clear fee line on the cart page with a running 'you need ₹X more for free delivery' bar
improvementIdeas.problem: Users and the regulator see fees as hidden; trust is low.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer complaints and checkout drop-offs, lower regulatory risk.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Checkout drop-off rate and fee complaints per 1,000 orders

improvementIdeas.idea: Café breakfast subscription: 5 or 20 coffees a month at a fixed price, pre-scheduled
improvementIdeas.problem: Café demand is spiky; Zepto wants daily habits.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Predictable morning orders, higher café margins, more daily active users.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Café orders per user per week and café gross margin

improvementIdeas.idea: Real-time stock sync so items out of stock are hidden before checkout
improvementIdeas.problem: Order cancellations after payment annoy users.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer cancellations and refunds, better trust.

improvementIdeas.idea: Self-serve ads dashboard for small D2C brands with fixed small budgets
improvementIdeas.problem: Ad revenue is key to profit; small brands find ads hard to buy.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More advertisers and higher ad revenue per order.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Number of active advertisers and ad revenue per order

improvementIdeas.idea: Freshness score shown on fruit and vegetable pages from past user ratings per store
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Pushes stores to improve quality and wins trust for fresh food.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Fresh repeat rate and freshness complaint rate

pmLessons: Growth is not the same as a healthy business. Zepto doubled revenue but investors still cut its value because it loses money on each order.
Small details change cost. Cutting average trip distance from 2.05 km to 1.83 km lowers delivery cost on every single order.
A new product line can change habits. Zepto Cafe turned a weekly grocery app into a daily one.
Being number two forces hard choices: spend to catch up, or slow down to save cash.
Short-term tricks like hidden fees can create long-term trust and legal problems.

interviewQuestions.question: Zepto needs to cut its loss per order from ₹79 to zero within a year. Where would you start?
interviewQuestions.hint: Break loss per order into revenue per order (margin, ads, fees) and cost per order (delivery, store, discounts). Pick the 2 biggest levers, like ad revenue and orders per store, and propose experiments with targets.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Zepto keep growing Zepto Cafe or focus on groceries?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare margins, habit-building (daily vs weekly use), operational complexity and food safety risks. Look at café attach rate and whether café users order more groceries.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you design Zepto Pass to be profitable?
interviewQuestions.hint: Price vs savings per user, free-delivery threshold, extra order frequency created vs discount cost. Test 2 to 3 price points and track incremental orders per member.

interviewQuestions.question: Blinkit has twice Zepto's stores. How should Zepto compete?
interviewQuestions.hint: Do not copy blindly. Pick cities where Zepto leads, focus on café and youth users, improve reliability, and spend only where store orders can reach profit.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you measure if a new dark store is succeeding?
interviewQuestions.hint: Orders per day vs break-even level, time to reach it, repeat rate of users in its area, on-time rate, and contribution margin per order.
